title.narrative: Green College Odisha: Creating Green Value Webs for Tribal Women Farmers

description.narrative: In total, the project reaches 9,250 people directly and 100,000 people indirectly in rural communities.A team of 60 main trainers (at least 25 women) trained by the Green College to train grassroots trainers in the main "green trades" such as agriculture, livestock/poultry, non-timber forest produce, fisheries, etc. and in institution building.1,200 Grassroot Workers from Odisha Livelihood Mission and government agencies -who will train the community members along with 200 resource persons from civil society organizations.4,000 ecopreneurs (50 % women) who are trained to start their own green business, from this group 400 people are selected who belong to the "rural youth with significant potential" (= High Potential Rural Youth - HPRY).70 key members of the NGO partners participating in APC 2.0600 local government officials from the Directorate of Horticulture, Department of Agriculture and Farmer Empowerment, Department of Mission Shakti and Odisha Livelihoods Mission (OLM) of the Government.120 board members from 30 producer companies and 2 to 3 members of 1,000 producer organizations are trained to manage companies sustainably and run the institutes with transparency and accountability.Indirect target groups:(1) 80,000 women farmers trained by the above-mentioned advisors;(2) 20,000 community members, belonging to the households of the above-mentioned 4,000 ecopreneurs, who will also benefit from the measures.

Overall objective : 80,000 women from remote tribal areas in the state Odisha in India, have improved livelihood opportunities from the green sector and entrepreneurship.Project objective: Extension workers, agricultural organisations and rural businesses have access to systematic knowledge management and capacity building and use their enhanced skills to generate effective livelihoods in the green sector in rural and indigenous areas in Odisha, India

The proposed project aims to foster green livelihoods and entrepreneurship in remote tribal areas of Odisha, with a strong focus on empowering women. Its primary goal is to establish a comprehensive learning, knowledge management, and capacity-building framework for the Agriculture Production Cluster (APC) project initiated by the Odisha government. The project will establish a state-level 'Green College' as a central hub to provide capacity building and technical support to stakeholders in developing sustainable Agriculture .It will address the capacity building needs of the APC by establishing a pool of local trainers (master trainers), the Green College can ensure standardized and high-quality training for producer companies, entrepreneurs and producer groups.
